source: ADR-0071's re-founding table, 2026-08-11 (#326), for the re-founded half (routing_classes); and, for the frozen pre-#326 half (classes), the human ruling on #258, 2026-08-06 as amended by #217 item 9, which still governs every process that has not fetched. A refusal citing a class id ADR-0071's table does not carry came from that frozen half, read by a process that predates #326 — the policy is not broken; see this file's compat key.
coverage: This table is not a complete account of what needs routing, and this sentence rides on a clear read as well as on a refusal, because the reader told nothing is wrong is the reader forming a belief about what was checked. Class 6 asserts an invariant no refusal enforces, and its path list names a minority of the gates this project runs; classes 4 and 5 refuse no route at all; classes 2 and 3 are bound to seats and so are checked at dispatch only, since a landing has no seat to check. A surface this file does not name is uncovered, never cleared, and a rung that did not run is not a rung that passed. Class ids 1 and 7 are retired by ADR-0071's re-founding table and are never reused, so an id is a stable historical handle rather than a position.
compat: Two documents live in this file for one transition window, and a parser reads exactly one of them. `routing_classes`, `routing_issue_exceptions` and `routing_route_exceptions` are the re-founded document and are read by every parser from #326 onward. `classes`, `issue_exceptions` and `route_exceptions` are the pre-#326 document, frozen verbatim as `origin/main` carried it at bbb6ade, and are read only by a `tools/routing_policy.py` that predates #326 — which is the copy an in-flight worktree's already-running `just land` or `just dispatch` imported before this landing. That older parser demands the ordered table 1..7 and cannot read a table with retired ids, so shipping only the re-founded half would refuse every in-flight landing and dispatch until each worktree rebased, on a remedy that sends the reader to repair a file that is not broken (#326, review round 3 claim 1). It is the argument `COVERAGE_UNSTATED` already makes about a newly-mandatory field, applied to the id shape it was not applied to. The frozen half governs only processes that have not fetched and is never consulted alongside the live half. Its removal is owned by #365, not before 2026-08-21. The condition this replaces — "once no worktree predating this landing is still in flight" — was withdrawn on arbitration because it is not computable: `just worktree list` sweeps registrations and this box carries over 150 of them, most long abandoned, so it would never have read true.

routing_classes.name: orchestration
routing_classes.label: Orchestration
routing_classes.remedy: Orchestration work goes to its route, and this row is founded on that route's seats rather than on a lane — a row admits the whole route, not its first step, the rule `tools/routing_policy.py` states over class 3 and #327's round 3 applied here: an issue declaring `Routing-class: orchestration` is refused taken by any seat outside the route that finishes that work, on every lane including Claude's. The route is `orchestrator`, which performs the act; `planner`, which plans it; `implementer`, which lands it (ruling 2 — the planner neither gates nor lands); `review`, which reviews that landing (ruling 4 — no change lands alone); and `recon`, admitted on #326 review round 3 claim 4's ground — a seat that authors, lands and reviews nothing cannot take the work, so refusing it protects nothing while barring a cheap read-only sweep. #327's second round appointed `orchestrator` alone and its third widened it (#327 review round 3, claim 1): the one-seat row left an orchestration issue plannable by nobody, landable by nobody, reviewable by nobody — ruling 4's reviewing instance was refused on every lane — and reconnoitrable by nobody, so #331, filed with this very marker, could have been dispatched only to the one seat that must not review its own landing. What the row refuses now is `retro` and `fable` and nothing else — the reading #327 review round 3's caveat asked its fixer to pick, on class 3's own ground, because the row copied does not supply one: both seats can take work and neither is a seat any landed ruling requires for this route, so the refusal still selects, where refusing `recon` selected nothing. That thinness is named rather than hidden: two seats left outside is evidence that the keep-on-Claude half was always the seat table's carve-out, and whether this row should be widened no further but deleted outright is the human's (#327 review round 3's recommendation to put exactly that to them). **Flagged, not silently overridden (#327 re-review of round 3, claim 3): `AGENTS.md`'s Model roles paragraph sends "process docs" to a `fable` seat, and `docs/agents/orchestration.md` — the orchestration seat's operating rules, by `AGENTS.md`'s own Orchestration seat section — is a process doc this row refuses to route there, the same conflict the ADR-authorship row below flags for its own subject. The sentence is stale rather than the row wrong — ADR-0071's seat map supersedes it in substance — and closing the overlap is #329's and #330's; until one of those lands the conflict stands on the record rather than in a commit message.** The keep-on-Claude half is not this row's — it is the seat table's carve-out (`orchestrator_claude_only` in `tools/dispatch.py`), the one provenance rule ADR-0071 ruling 1 left standing, provisional until the Codex orchestrator backup is built. Until #327's second round this row carried that half as a lane-selected refusal, which refused every seat on every non-Claude lane for an orchestration declaration while clearing the same declaration on Claude — broader than the carve-out it descended from, because its `seats: ["orchestrator"]` reads as scoping and `seats` is one evidence term, never a filter (#366 files the semantic). `required_seats` is the mechanism that actually scopes, so the row uses it. Checked at dispatch only, because a landing has no seat to check — this row carries no `landing_path_prefixes` for the same reason the ADR-authorship row carries none, and `parse_policy` refuses a seat-bound row that does, rather than letting the landing rung silently re-derive the lane bar. **Flagged, not silently overridden (#327 review round 2, claim 1): ADR-0071's re-founding table says this row "survives unchanged", and it no longer does — re-founding it on its seat is the fix that review directed, because the alternative was a second lane-selected provenance refusal the landing's prose had counted away; amending the ADR, or covering the departure with an ADR-0013 record, is the human's.**

routing_classes.name: adr_authorship
routing_classes.label: ADR authorship
routing_classes.remedy: Route ADR authorship to the three seats ADR-0071 rulings 2 and 4 require between them, on any lane including a non-Claude one: `planner` authors it, off the ordered profile preferences ruling 2 gives that seat; `implementer` lands it, because ruling 2's planner "neither gates nor lands"; and `review` reviews that landing, because ruling 4 lands no change alone. A row admitting the planner alone admitted nobody who could finish the work and refused the very review dispatch ruling 4 mandates — the deadlock found in #326 review round 2, claim 1 — so the admitted set is the whole route rather than its first step. `recon` is admitted beside those three and is not one of them (#326 review round 3, claim 4): it is read-only by description in `tools/dispatch.py`'s `SEATS`, so it authors, lands and reviews nothing, and refusing it defeats no purpose of a class that exists to stop an ADR being authored from a seat that cannot author one — the round that refused it applied the sufficiency rule ("admit every seat some ruling requires") as a necessity rule, which turns a capability requirement into a bar and routes a cheap read-only sweep to a seat that gates and lands. Its read-only standing is a description and not an enforced `permission_mode`, so the admission rests on what that seat is for, and a `recon` seat that gained write powers would need this row revisited. Refused on every lane including Claude's: `orchestrator` is class 2's seat, `fable` is none of the seats rulings 2 and 4 require for this route — the #300 retro allowance that once carried it to ADR work was superseded by ADR-0071's trailer and deleted with the ladder it suspended (#327), so what refuses it here is seating and not provenance — and `retro` files and lands nothing under ruling 3 — the retro half of the class this row descends from is withdrawn by that ruling, along with its `docs/process-log.md` path. **Flagged, not silently overridden (#326 review round 3, claim 5): `AGENTS.md`'s Model roles paragraph — the file an agent actually reads before dispatching, and `CLAUDE.md` is the committed symlink to it — still sends "anything touching ADRs" to a `fable` seat, which this row refuses.** ADR-0071 ruling 2 supersedes that mapping in substance, so the sentence is stale rather than this row wrong, and `SEATS` records that closing the overlap is #329's and #330's; until one of those lands the conflict stands on the record rather than in a commit message. That is what ruling 1 means by eligibility ceasing to be a property of provenance — a lane-selected refusal here would have refused `codex`/`codex-sol-xhigh`/`planner`, the first entry in the list this remedy prescribes, while clearing any Claude seat whatever. The class is therefore enforced where a seat exists, which is dispatch. `just land` is handed a lane and a diff and no seat, so this row carries no landing prefixes and the landing rung does not test it — an ADR reaching `origin/main` from an unappointed seat is uncaught, not cleared. **Two departures from ADR-0071's re-founding table, both labelled (#326 review round 2, claim 3; #326 review round 3, claim 9).** The first is a conflict: ADR-0071's re-founding table prescribes `docs/adr/` as this row's landing path and this row has none, because a seat-bound row carrying landing prefixes would clear at dispatch for the seat it appoints and then refuse that same route at landing, where no seat is knowable, so the two cannot both hold as written; whether the ADR is amended or an ADR-0013 record covers it is the human's. The second is a synthesis rather than a conflict, and is named so a reader auditing this row against the ADR is not left to spot it: the table binds this class "to the planner's list rather than to Claude", and this row admits four seats. Read literally that is the deadlock — the planner neither gates nor lands — so the row is read together with rulings 2 and 4, whose seats it names above. A reader who thinks the literal words should have won has the departure in front of them rather than buried in a commit message.

routing_classes.name: plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green
routing_classes.label: The #181 shape
issue_phrases: plausible wrong fix would also have gone green
plausible wrong fix would also go green
routing_classes.remedy: No mechanical gate distinguishes this diagnosis's plausible wrong fix from the right one, so the remedy is capability rather than provenance: route it to the `planner` seat and escalate. ADR-0071 ruling 5's fourth transferring-escalation condition, `plausible_wrong_fix_goes_green`, fires on exactly this class and names the transfer; the condition and its remedy are data in `config/escalation-conditions.json` and reach an agent as an emission.

routing_classes.name: in_world_landings
routing_classes.label: In-world landings
routing_classes.remedy: A subagent cannot hold the full `just regress` corpus's foreground wait — `.claude/hooks/deny-subagent-waits.py` denies it — so a seat reached as a subagent cannot gate its own in-world work and must not take it. That is the whole of the rule: `just dispatch` launches a top-level session, which the wait hook permits by returning 0 where there is no agent id, so this row refuses no dispatch route. Its two path lists remain the one authority for what an in-world surface is, read by `just land`'s corpus rung, `tools/admission.py` and `tools/brief.py` (#302).

routing_classes.name: gates_themselves
routing_classes.label: The gates themselves
routing_classes.remedy: Two rules live on this row and they are not the same rule, so read which one refused you. The **invariant** is the conflict of interest — no instance authors the gate that judges it — and it binds every instance, Claude's included; it is discharged by an independent review under ADR-0071 ruling 4, and **no refusal enforces it** until #331's never-alone exemption list lands — the ADR's sequencing step 7 — so today it is asserted and honoured by procedure. The **refusal** you have actually met is the older keep-on-Claude bar, still selected by lane: a non-Claude lane is refused these paths and the Claude lane is exempt. It is kept, and the label kept with it, because retiring it before the exemption list exists would leave the gates with neither rule; it is not evidence that the invariant was checked, and a Claude landing here has cleared nothing. The half of the invariant that is enforceable today is enforced: this class carries no exception, and the withdrawn `Routing-exception: proposal-only` marker went with the framing, because an instance that can except itself from the gate that judges it is precisely the shape being forbidden. `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/settings.json` are here, not dropped: they are the denial layer and the permission allowlist, and the withdrawn gated-semantic-surfaces class was the only routing rule that named them. Coverage is incomplete: the list names six tools plus those two paths, and omits `tools/check_adr_form.py`, `tools/check_seat_config.py`, `tools/check_validated_markers.py`, `tools/check_conflict_markers.py`, `tools/check_source_symlink.py`, `tools/check_sqf_bans.py`, `tools/generate_seats.py` and `tools/export_command_schema.py` — the eight `just check` reaches — and `tools/breaker.py`, which no `check-*` recipe runs and which `just breaker` and `just watch-report` reach instead (review round 2 claim 4, correcting both this clause and ADR-0071's own row 6, which made the same slip) — along with every gate reached only through `just unit`, `just mutation`, `just land` and `just regress`. A diff touching a gate this list does not name is uncovered, never cleared.
